messages:
ashley (acct-exec): Hey team — POC customer hit a hard blocker. Their integration intermittently returns an extra trailing payload after the JSON blob when using our function-calling/structured output mode. Seeing downstream parse failures in their app. Can we swarm?

sam (sales-engineer): Ugh. Any sample response? model + endpoint + whether they used streaming?

ashley (acct-exec): They sent a snippet:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "choices": [ { "message": { "name": "extract", "arguments": "{\"id\": 123, \"items\": [\"a\", \"b\"]}" } } ]
}
--partial-binary--

// client-side JSON.parse fails because of trailing garbage
```
They're calling /v1/generate with json_mode and function schema enabled. Not always, maybe after a retry. Also got a 429 once with X-Request-Id: req_9b2f.

tyler (ml-eng): Thanks. Two quick asks: can you get the full request_id from the customer for the 429? And what model variant + quant/beam settings? Could be post-processing or streaming boundary mixing.

ashley (acct-exec): I'll ask. Customer said model = redwood-medium-v1, streaming=false, max_tokens=512, but they do client-side retries on 500/429.

prashant (infra): If client retries while our backend is still streaming/finishing the previous chunk it could produce a concatenated payload on the TCP connection in rare cases. Need request ids to map. ops-bot, any infra traces?

ops-bot: Trace created: link=https://internal.traces/replay/req_9b2f, span=span_7f3a. Associated logs: [req_9b2f, req_9b2g].

tyler (ml-eng): Opening a debug job: please forward the customer's exact raw response (including headers). Also share whether they use gzip or chunked. If they post retries with keep-alive and re-used connection, we might be hitting a connection boundary bug where we append leftover bytes after the JSON stream.

sam (sales-engineer): Also they're asking about pricing impact if we recommend disabling client-side retries and instead use our built-in retry/backoff at the SDK level. Can we give a one-liner?

prashant (infra): One-liner: removing aggressive retries reduces duplicate token costs — estimate depends on retry rate. For POC with 10% retry rate we could save ~10% token spend but add latency risk. For enterprise we can enable idempotency keys and SDK-level de-dup to avoid double-cost.

ashley (acct-exec): Customer also filled out the security questionnaire asking about request logging during POC — they want assurance we won't persist raw prompt+outputs beyond 30 days. Is that configurable on Dedicated?

prashant (infra): Yes, for Dedicated you can set retention and disable prompt logging; for hosted we can opt into limited retention under an enterprise contract. I'll loop in compliance.

tyler (ml-eng): Back to the parse failure: two mitigation suggestions for the customer while we debug: 1) switch to streaming=true and parse as stream (safer for large payloads), or 2) add a defensive sanitizer that extracts the first top-level JSON object with a regex before JSON.parse. Neither ideal, but quick.

sam (sales-engineer): Can we also provide them a short SDK patch they can drop-in which validates complete response using Content-Length / transfer-encoding sanity checks?

prashant (infra): I'll paste a tiny node patch they can use:
```js
// quick sanity wrapper
async function safeParse(respText) {
  const idx = respText.indexOf('\n}\'); // naive find end of object - adjust for real world
  if (idx === -1) return JSON.parse(respText);
  const candidate = respText.slice(0, idx + 2);
  return JSON.parse(candidate);
}
```
(not production ready, but helps triage)

tyler (ml-eng): Also asked infra to check our HTTP server logs for any keep-alive connection reuse edgecases. Prashant, ops-bot flagged two nearby request ids req_9b2f and req_9b2g — can you correlate to worker ids and kernel logs?

ops-bot: Correlation: req_9b2f -> worker-22 (gpu-a100-3), req_9b2g -> worker-22 as well. Both show close timestamps 2026-03-19T14:12:03Z and 2026-03-19T14:12:05Z. There's one WARN: "stream-terminate: leftover-bytes" at 14:12:05.

tyler (ml-eng): That WARN is the smoking gun. Likely our stream flush didn't clear buffer before closing connection when a retry occurred. I'll send a quick patch to add a trailing newline delimiter for JSON-mode responses to avoid clients accidentally concatenating.

sam (sales-engineer): Customer wants ETA — how long to patch + rollout?

prashant (infra): Hotfix to worker shim to append canonical delimiter ("\n---\n") will take ~2-4 hours to test in staging, then safe canary to 10% in 2 hours, full rollout next day pending no regression.

ashley (acct-exec): I'll tell customer: we're prioritizing this, hotfix in staging today, canary tomorrow, will give them a temporary SDK snippet to sanitize and offer to enable Dedicated retention controls for logs.

sam (sales-engineer): Thanks. Also capture pricing note and QA for security questionnaire. I'll follow up with customer on call at 17:00 PT.

tyler (ml-eng): After hotfix we'll still add an integration test that simulates client retries + keep-alive connections to prevent regression.

ashley (acct-exec): Perfect. I'll post customer's raw response when they send it. :thumbsup:
